title: Einstein Hooks v3 Evolve
subtitle: LP economics, tested on mainnet
question: Over a real weekend, does an LP in a BELL pool end up with more value than an LP in a plain Uniswap v4 pool with the same capital and range?

design.capital: the same USD amount in both pools, same ticks, seeded in the same block or the next
flow: organic: swaps from outside wallets, counted as they come
controlled: one public bot trades both pools toward the same reference price with the same logic and the same maximum size

referencePrice.source: Chainlink NVDA feed on Robinhood Chain (latestRoundData)
referencePrice.perSwap: The live feed round when it is at most 6 hours old at the swap. Otherwise the first round the feed publishes after the swap, which is the reopen price. The feed holds its last price over a weekend, so a stale read is never used as if it were fresh.
referencePrice.start: The feed at the window start block.
referencePrice.end: The feed at the last block at or before Monday 10:00 ET. It must be a fresh round, or claim E3 does not pass.

metrics.feesEarned: For every Swap event: input amount times the event fee, times the position's share of pool liquidity (zero when the pool tick is outside its range). Fees paid in NVDA are valued at the end reference price.
metrics.lvr: For every Swap event: (reference price minus execution price, with the fee taken out) times the NVDA the swapper received, times the position's share. A negative number means the LP gained.
metrics.valueVsHold: Position value at the end price, plus fees earned, minus the starting tokens valued at the end price. Position value is the liquidity's token amounts at the last Swap event's price.
metrics.netLpResult: valueVsHold, in bps of starting capital. The headline is BELL minus control, in bps of capital.
metrics.blockedFlow: Swaps the BELL pool refused, each linked to its reverted transaction with the error name.

limits: One asset and one weekend per run. Not a guarantee for every market or every weekend.
Part of the flow comes from a controlled bot, labelled separately from organic flow.
The control is one fixed fee tier (30 bps). Other tiers could do better or worse.
If BELL loses a run, the page says so in the verdict line.
Not an audit and not financial advice.
notAllowed: changing the reference price after the fact
leaving out a session that looks bad

claims.title: Both pools are set up the same way
claims.proof: Initialize and seed transactions for both, position ids, ticks and amounts.
claims.passes: Capital within 1 USDG, same ticks, seeded within 2 blocks.

claims.title: The control pool has no hook
claims.proof: The control pool key, read from its Initialize event.
claims.passes: Hook address is the zero address.

claims.title: The reference price is fixed and public
claims.proof: The Chainlink round id and price at Monday 10:00 ET, recorded in proof.json.
claims.passes: The replay reads the same round, and it is fresh.

claims.title: Fees are counted correctly
claims.proof: Every Swap event of both pools in the window.
claims.passes: The replay total equals the page total.

claims.title: LVR is counted correctly
claims.proof: Per swap, reference price against execution price.
claims.passes: The replay total equals the page total.

claims.title: Net LP result is correct
claims.proof: End position value against hold, read at the end block.
claims.passes: The replay result equals the page result.

claims.title: The bot treated both pools the same
claims.proof: Bot source code, its hash, and every bot transaction.
claims.passes: Same source and the same maximum size on both pools, every transaction listed.

claims.title: BELL refused toxic flow
claims.proof: The list of reverted transactions with their error names.
claims.passes: Every revert is linked and replays with its error.

claims.title: Anyone can replay it
claims.passes: Prints PASS for E1 to E8.
